title: Use Case Solutions

toc.text: UC2 — Financial services compliance + churn alert (worked solution)
UC4 — Manufacturing unified account + P1 escalation (worked solution)

html:
The final phase closes the loop: full worked solutions for UC1–UC4 from Phase 17, delivered end-to-end (sources → identity → transforms → segmented → activated → actioned), a grading rubric to score your own attempt, and the capstone mini-project that assembles all four patterns into one design. This is the last checkpoint before the Data-Con-101 exam.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Grade your Phase 17 attempt against worked solutions using a sharable rubric.
  • Produce complete, justified architectures for retail, finance, telco/health, and manufacturing cases.
  • Wire any of the four patterns into this repo's Apex/objects/actions.
  • Confidently answer "what would you configure now?" on a scenario question.

UC1 — Retail omnichannel win-back (worked solution)

Answer sentence: Ingest ERP orders (CSV connector, nightly) + web events (Ingestion API, streaming) + MC sends (MC connector) into the Order__dlm/Web_Event__dlm/Engagement__dlm DLOs; unify under IndividualId (email + loyalty ID resolution); transform Recency (days since last order), OrderCount == 5+, Tier == Gold; build segment "Win-Back Eligible"; publish via MCE activation to a data extension with {Email, Tier, Recency, IncentiveCode} attributes; MCE journey uses the DE as entry source; consent Email filter applied at activation.

StepConfiguration
ERP orders → DLOSalesforce CSV dataset (nightly)
Web events → DLOIngestion API, streaming (real-time for the intent kicker)
MC sends → DLOMarketing Cloud connector
IdentityEmail + loyalty-ID match rule → IndividualId
TransformRecency = NOW() - last order; OrderCount; profile Tier
Insight(optional) WebIntentScore for real-time kicker
SegmentGold AND OrderCount >= 5 AND Recency >= 60 (static, daily refresh)
ActivationMCE → data extension; attributes = 4; refresh = scheduled daily
ConsentEmail category filter at activation (ActivationSyncService shows 3/2 math)
Data spaceMarketing space sees only the activation attribute DE; purchasing history stays in its own space

Why the split: CRM/service space holds order history (service may see it); marketing space holds the DE + attributes. Rule: activate attributes, don't share the table.

UC2 — Financial services compliance + churn alert (worked solution)

Answer sentence: Ingest 3 legacy sources (core nightly, cards real-time, loans daily) into Account__ or Individual__dlm DLOs; unify on official ID + tax ID; build BalanceTrend, SpendVelocity, ChurnScore (Einstein model deployed as profile attribute); enforce channel-isolated consent; segment "At-Risk Gold" → data action updates the Case/priority; Agentforce assistant answers from a data space with card limits excluded.

StepConfiguration
IdentityOfficial ID + tax ID match rules (highest confidence)
InsightsChurnScore from Einstein Studio model (Phase 13), BalanceTrend, SpendVelocity
ConsentCategories Email/SMS/Push separate; single withdrawal respected via Consent_Preference__c
SegmentTier == Gold AND ChurnScore >= 0.6
Activation/ActionData action → Case update/priority (UC2b) + notify servicing team
AgentforceAgent grounded on data space WITHOUT card limits (field-level security)
RetentionCards DLO 90d; core 7y; audit artifacts (activation runs, consent captures) retained
LineageRetention + lineage to satisfy regulator ("where did this score come from?")

UC3 — Telco/Healthcare 360 self-service (worked solution)

Answer sentence: Unify billing + usage + tickets + warranty PDFs into a Unified Individual + a Data Graph; present on-the-fly via Data 360 console components (no write-back); Agentforce assistant uses a retriever over warranty/SLA documents + an Apex action for live account data, all inside the self-service data space (promo consent separate).

StepConfiguration
Files (warranty PDFs, SLA docs)File ingestion → indexed for retrieval (Phase 13)
Live account dataApex action (AgentforceBillingContextService pattern, Phase 14) — narrow JSON node
Console viewData 360 components/related list — on-the-fly, no CRM field copies
Agent groundingRetriever (hybrid search over PDFs + docs) + prompt merge fields + RAG fallback
Data spaceSelf-service: own account + warranty/SLA docs ONLY; promo consent activation separate
ConsentDisplay ≠ marketing; only the activation path is consent-gated

The distinction to say aloud: display is on-the-fly component + grounding; activation is consent-gated publish. Mixing the two is the classic wrong answer.

UC4 — Manufacturing unified account + P1 escalation (worked solution)

Answer sentence: Ingest ERP order files (hourly) + IoT telemetry (streaming) + cases (CRM); resolve device serial → AccountId (resolution on telemetry); compute a real-time Maintenance_Score calculated insight (threshold > 80) on streaming data; the crossing fires a data action → Case priority P1 + webhook notification to field manager; dispatch views segment "Flash Maintenance" — all streaming end-to-end.

StepConfiguration
IoT telemetryStreaming (Ingestion API / streaming dataset) — REQUIRED for real-time
Telemetry → accountDevice-serial match into account hierarchy (account unification)
InsightMaintenance_Score real-time calculated insight, threshold = 80 (Phase 5)
ActionData action → Case P1 + webhook (external target; correlation-id idempotency)
Segment"Flash Maintenance" (dynamic) for dispatch console
The proofEvery hop streaming: ingestion → transform → insight → dynamic segment → action

Trap avoided: if telemetry is ingested nightly, the P1 reacts in days. The C-S-T-A constraint in UC4 is the real-time chain, and the candidate answer that "fixes the report" is wrong — the fix is making ingestion streaming.

Grading rubric (score your Phase 17 attempt)

Score each: 0 = absent, 1 = partial, 2 = correct & justified.

CriterionWhat earns 2
Sources & connectors namedCorrect connector per source (shared quota, streaming flags)
Identity rules correctRight match attributes + confidence; cross-object key set
Transforms/insights chosenCalculated insight vs segment used correctly (Phases 5/6)
Segment definition completeCriteria + refresh type (static vs dynamic) justified
Activation/action target rightMCE-DE vs CRM vs webhook chosen with justification
Data-space/consent/retentionBoundary + suppression + retention applied to the right hop
Real-time disciplineAll hops streaming or the breaking hop identified
Apex/objects tie-inMaps to this repo (services/triggers/flows)

Target: ≥ 6/8 with a stated-but-not-perfect area, then re-attempt UC2 and UC4 from scratch.

Capstone: the "one-design" challenge

Design ONE integrated architecture that serves all four UCs from one shared platform:

  • One identity spine (IndividualId), two unified profiles (Individual + Account), four data spaces (RetailOps, RisOps, SelfService, Manufacturing).
  • Shared service assets from this repo: ConsentManagementService (single withdrawal), IdentityResolutionHelperService, DataCloudReportingService KPI layer, DataActionHandlerService + Data_Action_Event__e.
  • State the three hops where "data in the wrong space" would be the compliance disaster, and the three hops where a batch would break a real-time promise.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Score your Phase 17

Score UC1 and UC3 against the rubric. Rewrite the weaker one in one paragraph.

Exercise 2: The speaking test

Explain UC2 to a non-technical stakeholder in 60 seconds: the 4 phrases you would use (unified profile, churn score, consent-isolated channels, grounded agent). Practice until smooth.

Exercise 3: Repo wiring

Map UC4 to code: which service + trigger + flow (by name in this repo) implements each of its 5 hops. Add a one-line comment per mapping to ARCHITECTURE.md.

Exercise 4: Exam simulation

Set 40 minutes. Answer UC1 + UC3 + one 5-question domain quiz from Phase 15. Self-grade with the rubric.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Worked solutionFull architecture (sources→action) with justifications for the correct config.
Activate attributes, don't share the tableData-space + activation-attribute discipline (UC1).
Channel-isolated consentSeparate categories per channel; single withdrawal respected everywhere.
Real-time chainStreaming ingestion → streaming insight → dynamic segment → streaming action.
On-the-fly display ≠ activationConsole components/grounding vs consent-gated publishing (UC3).

Certification Checkpoints (final)

  • I can score a use case with the 8-criterion rubric and hit ≥ 6/8.
  • I can explain all four UCs in ≤ 60 seconds each to a business audience.
  • I can map every UC hop to this repo's Apex/triggers/flows.
  • I can design a single-platform architecture with correct data-space separation.
  • I am ready for the Data-Con-101 exam (mocks ≥ 75%, specs cold).

Self-Check (final)

  1. Q: Expose the account's lifetime order value to a marketing segment — table or attributes? — A: Activation attributes only (leaf-level attributes on the activation to the MCE DE); the order table stays in the ops space.
  2. Q: "Can't have the assistant tell me my card limit" — which two layers? — A: Data-space scoping (limit to the self-service space) + field-level security inside the space; the grounding components inherit both.
  3. Q: The churn journey must fire within 15 minutes of the score crossing. — A: Streaming telemetry → streaming Maintenance/Churn calculated insight → dynamic segment → data action, all streaming; verify no batch hop.
  4. Q: How do you prove lineage "where did ChurnScore come from"? — A: Data 360 lineage trail (source → DLO → DMO → model → profile attribute → segment → activation) + retained audit artifacts.
